scope: THE JOIN ONLY. This is not a re-review of either subject; two other lanes hold those and are writing their own verdict files. Findings below are stated as properties of the PAIR, and every one names a JSON pointer in each artifact. Where a finding is also visible as a single-artifact defect, that is noted so the coordinator can deduplicate against the subject lanes.

verdictBasis.statement: The join does NOT close. Of doctor's four consentable action classes, ONE (CA-4 egress) resolves to a DR-105 token; ONE (CA-1) resolves only for its subprocess half; and TWO (CA-2, CA-3) require tokens DR-105 deliberately RESERVED or EXCLUDED, so they are unexercisable under this vocabulary permanently rather than pending a cardinality decision. Doctor's fail-closed rule then makes them CONSENT-REQUIRED forever. In the opposite direction, four DR-105 tokens land on doctor's UNCONSENTED DEFAULT posture, which doctor gates with nothing. The mandated scenario walks do not produce one deterministic answer.
verdictBasis.whatThisVerdictIsNOT: It is NOT a finding that either artifact overclaimed. Neither asserts the join closes: doctor keeps consentRecord.permissionRef a RESERVED BINDING POINT and DR-105 keeps PT-NET-EGRESS's slice-1 posture riding DR-114. The incoherence is a DESIGN GAP BETWEEN two blind-authored contracts, plus one non-replicating recital (CONTRA-8). Both artifacts are unusually honest about their own reach; the pair still does not compose.
verdictBasis.acceptGate: ACCEPT requires ZERO surviving blockers. SEVEN blockers survive independent measurement. Verdict is INCOHERENT and the pair must not be applied together as it stands.
verdictBasis.rootCause: ACTOR MISMATCH, never named on either side. Every DR-105 token is a COMPONENT permission whose authorization record originates in an admitted manifest's permissions[] block (/truthTables/tables/0/rows/*/REQUESTED: 'The admitted manifest's `permissions[]` block names this token with a reason ... there is no runtime path by which a component asks for a token its manifest did not declare'). Doctor is a HOST surface with no manifest, no component generation, and no broker channel of its own. DR-105's own fourth deliberate non-token (/permissionVocabulary/deliberateNonTokens/3) rules that a host acting 'under the invoking user's direct instruction on the command line' is NOT a permissioned actor at all -- which is an exact description of doctor's CA-1..CA-4. Doctor meanwhile requires (/consentModel/dr105Join/theJoinExactly/cardinalityIsDr105s) that the mapping be TOTAL over all four classes. The two positions cannot both hold, and neither artifact states which it means.

blockers.oneLine: CA-2 (customer tool execution) requires the general execute-anything grant DR-105 deliberately withheld and the third-party execution DR-105 EXCLUDED; it is permanently unexercisable, taking the DECIDED D-008/DR-119 customer-owned-external-system exception down with it.

CA-3 (probes) spans four effects, of which none has a token: keychain is RESERVED (DR-108 deferred), local socket / named pipe is RESERVED, out-of-root path read is not in the vocabulary at all, privileged platform facility is unnamed.

Doctor's CLOSED five-token check-status set and CLOSED three-value execution vocabulary cannot carry DR-105's INDETERMINATE or COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, which DR-105 requires be disclosed as OUTCOMES and forbids being modeled as refusals.

DR-105's journal-every-acceptance rule collides mechanically with doctor's FC-RO byte-immutability fixture; the grant journal's state class is expressly undetermined (ID-DEP-P5), so the two acceptance fixtures can both run and disagree.

Circular deferral on the one question the join turns on: DR-105 /tensionsObserved/2 defers 'is a doctor consent a journal grant?' to DR-114's owner; doctor /consentModel/dr105Join/whatThisContractDoesNotDefine/2 defers grant-revocation linearization to DR-105. Revoke-mid-probe has two answers and no selector.

Four DR-105 tokens (FS-READ-PROJECT, FS-READ-COMPONENT, FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE, ENV-READ) describe effects doctor performs in its UNCONSENTED default posture; doctor references none of them, so doctor's 'default' is a permissioned action set under DR-105's tables while being ungated in doctor's.

MEASUREMENT: doctor /whatThisDoesNotDo/2 asserts 'no DR-105 artifact exists in the measured tree'. False at current bytes and contradicted by doctor's own /recordedInputs/lateMeasurementObservation, which exists precisely to prevent this.

gaps.title: No DR-105 token has a doctor-side authorization origin: the REQUESTED column cannot be instantiated for any doctor action
gaps.measurement: DR-105's REQUESTED column is defined solely as 'A declaration in the admitted manifest', with 'no runtime path by which a component asks for a token its manifest did not declare'. Doctor's only two admissible consent carriers are explicit invocation-time naming and pre-existing policy; neither is a manifest, and doctor has no manifest of its own. Additionally doctor's expresslyNotAdmissible list (/consentModel/howConsentIsNamed/expresslyNotAdmissible/3) forbids 'a component or manifest granting itself the consent' -- the manifest route is the one DR-105 supplies and the one doctor forbids.
gaps.consequence: The join cannot begin at the first column of DR-105's own table. Every finding below is a consequence of this one.
gaps.closesBy: A joint disposition naming whether host surfaces are subject to the vocabulary and, if so, what plays the manifest's role for them.

gaps.title: CA-1's in-process half has no token
gaps.measurement: Doctor CA-1 covers 'Spawning an admitted component's executable, OR running component code in-process'. PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED's meaning is bounded to 'as a child process'. DR-105 treats in-host-process as a TABLE AXIS (/truthTables/executionModes/modes/in-host-process), not as a grantable act, and mints no token for loading component code into the host address space.
gaps.consequence: If V2 admits the in-host mode (ID-DEP-P10, DR-105's own gating dependency, which notes the pinned prototype places exactly this slice's components there), CA-1's realised form is the half with no token. Doctor's fail-closed rule renders COMPONENT-LIVENESS unexercisable in that mode.

gaps.title: CA-3's out-of-root path read has no token and is not even a reserved point
gaps.measurement: CA-3 covers 'stat-ing or reading a path outside the install and project roots'. PT-FS-READ-PROJECT is bounded 'inside the project root ... symlink targets are resolved before the containment test, so a link inside the root that resolves outside is outside'. PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT is bounded to 'the component's own immutable installed tree'. No third read token exists and no reserved extension point covers arbitrary-path reads (reserved fs point is fs.write.project only, /permissionVocabulary/reservedExtensionPoints/0).
gaps.consequence: By DR-105's closure rule the effect is denied by absence and a declaration of it decides PR-3 / UNKNOWN_PERMISSION_TOKEN. CA-3's most ordinary case is unexercisable with no minting owner named.

gaps.title: CA-3's 'querying a privileged platform facility' has no token and only a partial reserved point
gaps.measurement: Reserved point 5 covers 'inbound network / listening sockets, IPC endpoints, device and accelerator access'. A 'privileged platform facility' query is not obviously any of these and is not enumerated elsewhere; DR-105's coverageObligation 'other effects' cell (/coverageObligation/mapping/other effects) mints only PT-ENV-READ and PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED there.
gaps.consequence: Undecidable whether this case is RESERVED (a scheduling problem) or ABSENT (a closure-rule refusal). The pair does not say.

gaps.title: Doctor's consent record cannot instantiate DR-105's grant binding tuple
gaps.measurement: DR-105 binds a grant to a '(component, generation, process instance, operation, grant, project, scope, expiry)' tuple and AUD binds 'acceptance, effect-commit, revocation, cleanup, and residual outcome, each bound to the grant generation, the process descendant, the Run/operation, and the broker request IDs'. Doctor's consent record has ten members (id, actionClass, permissionRef, scope, endpoint, bytes, authorization, execution, result, residualLimitation); none is a grant, generation, process instance, project, operation, or expiry, and the target identity is carried inside the free-text 'scope' member. Doctor additionally mints NO identity by rule (/identityDependencies/9 ID-DEP-10).
gaps.consequence: Even under the reading most favourable to the join (doctor consent IS a journal grant), doctor cannot supply the identities DR-105's audit binding requires, and DR-105 supplies none of them either (ID-DEP-P12 parks them at DR-006).

misses.title: PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE -- doctor's one permitted write is unreferenced
misses.measurement: Doctor DP-1: 'The one exception is the Operational metadata class doctor is the declared owner of ... doctor writes only its own audit/journal record of having run'. FC-RO's pass property admits exactly those bytes changing. PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE is minted for 'Create, modify, or remove bytes inside the host-owned state namespace allocated to this component for its declared state class', with the declared state class deferred to DR-124 -- the same DR-124 doctor rides at ID-DEP-7 for the same class.
misses.note: The token's own words say 'allocated to this COMPONENT', so the token as written does not cover a host surface's write either. This is a MISS on doctor's side and a coverage hole on DR-105's side simultaneously.
misses.consequence: Doctor's sole mutation is unpermissioned in doctor and unexpressible in DR-105.

misses.title: PT-FS-READ-PROJECT and PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT -- doctor's default reads are unreferenced
misses.measurement: Doctor core mode reads installed generation inventory, core-owned state, component index custody records and admitted manifest metadata; project mode additionally resolves strict configuration and reads the project lock. DR-105 mints exactly these two tokens as 'the local read half of D-002's own DR-105 scoping'. Doctor references neither.
misses.note: PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT is bounded to 'the component's OWN immutable installed tree'; doctor reads OTHER components' trees and index records, which the token as written does not express. Again a MISS and a coverage hole at once.

misses.title: PT-ENV-READ -- the pair's ONLY enforced-by-construction token, and doctor reads the environment layer without naming it
misses.measurement: Doctor resolves 'host configuration layers 1, 2 and 5 (compiled defaults, user-global settings, allowlisted environment)'. PT-ENV-READ is the token for reading the environment block and holds 2 of the table's 4 enforced cells; its named mechanism is 'the `envp` argument to execve(2) / the environment array passed to posix_spawn(3)' -- a mechanism operated by a PARENT on a CHILD.
misses.consequence: Doctor is the parent. Nobody constructs doctor's envp. The single enforced mechanism in the whole 28-cell table is un-instantiable for the surface the token's slice-1 posture was written for.

misses.title: PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED -- doctor forgoes the one route DR-105 can actually enforce
misses.measurement: CA-1 restricts the wire to control-plane F-2 and F-4 only, never `select`, and never `effectRequest`. PT-HOST-EFFECT-BROKERED is the only token whose child-process cells carry ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, and its refusal is 'total FOR THAT ROUTE'.
misses.consequence: Not a defect on its own -- doctor's probes are host-initiated, so the broker is arguably backwards for them -- but it means the joined pair contains ZERO enforced cells reachable by any doctor action. Worth the coordinator's attention because it makes 'consent' in the joined design purely disclosive.

misses.title: PR-7 and doctor's CONSENT-REQUIRED are the same decision under two unbound names
misses.measurement: PR-7 'consent-required-and-unavailable' covers 'Trusted-code fallback or a consented probe/egress is needed and no consent exists'. Doctor's CONSENT-REQUIRED status is 'the honest name for we did not look' when consent was not named. Measured: zero occurrences of `PR-[1-9]` in doctor's bytes; zero occurrences of `CA-[1-4]` in DR-105's bytes.
misses.consequence: Doctor declares (/consentModel/consentableActionClasses/0/protocolShape) that it 'mints no refusal family of its own' and rides RF-1..RF-8. DR-105 declares PR-n REFINE RF-6 and that one RF-6 carries exactly one PR-n. Doctor's CONSENT-REQUIRED reaches no RF-6 at all (there is no brokered request), so its decision class is unbound in both directions.

contradictions.title: CA-2 requires exactly the execute-anything grant DR-105 refused, and the third-party execution DR-105 EXCLUDED
contradictions.measurement: Doctor CA-2 covers 'Executing a customer-owned external tool or platform facility', bound to 'the exact DECLARED external-system identity from the manifest'. PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED is bounded to 'a program that the admitted manifest declared, FROM INSIDE the component's own admitted immutable tree', and its justification states that this restriction 'is what keeps it from becoming a general execute-anything grant, which freeze law 11 (file 03, repository-code execution default) forbids by default'. Separately, reserved point 6 states 'third-party / untrusted component execution of any kind -- EXCLUDED, not reserved-for-this-lane', citing the DR-105 row's own consequence column, with minting assigned to DR-117/DR-128 product approval, explicitly 'not this contract'.
contradictions.whyThisIsAContradictionAndNotACardinalit: Doctor's escape hatch (/consentModel/dr105Join/theJoinExactly/cardinalityIsDr105s -- 'Whether an action class maps to exactly one DR-105 token, to several, or to a token plus a scope expression is DR-105's to decide') cannot help: no number of DR-105 tokens composes into a grant DR-105 states it will never mint.
contradictions.productConsequence: Doctor's own fail-closed rule makes CA-2 UNEXERCISABLE. Doctor is the named carrier of the DECIDED D-008 / DR-119 customer-owned-external-system exception, which file 02 requires to appear 'in manifest and doctor output' with 'typed absence/failure behavior' (doctor /identityDependencies/8 ID-DEP-9). Applying this pair ships a doctor that must report CONSENT-REQUIRED for a requirement the corpus has already ACCEPTED.
contradictions.routeTo: The DR-105 row's owner jointly with DR-117/DR-128, or a DR-114 successor that removes CA-2 from the consent model and routes the customer-tool case elsewhere.

contradictions.title: CA-3 covers keychain reads; secret-handle is RESERVED-NOT-MINTED and DR-108 is deferred out of slice 1 by D-002
contradictions.measurement: CA-3 covers 'reading an OS keychain entry'. DR-105: 'secret-handle access -- RESERVED, not minted ... D-002 defers DR-108 explicitly (no credential-requiring features in slice 1). Minting the token here would design against a deferred row.' Minting owner is DR-108's closure.
contradictions.consequence: A doctor consent class whose named example is a deferred-row effect. Under doctor's fail-closed rule this branch of CA-3 is unexercisable until DR-108 closes, which D-002 has already put outside slice 1.

contradictions.title: CA-3 covers opening a local socket or named pipe; IPC endpoints are RESERVED-NOT-MINTED
contradictions.measurement: CA-3 covers 'opening a local socket or named pipe'. DR-105 reserved point 5: 'inbound network / listening sockets, IPC endpoints, device and accelerator access -- RESERVED, not minted ... No measured source in D-002's slice names a component that listens, binds an IPC endpoint, or touches a device.' Doctor names exactly such a surface, and DR-105 did not measure it because doctor's contract did not exist when DR-105 measured file 04.
contradictions.note: The absence claim DR-105 bases the reservation on is bounded to the pinned prototype and to measured V2 sources; doctor's CA-3 is a V2 source that post-dates the measurement. Recorded as ENVIRONMENT-adjacent in origin but as a genuine JOIN contradiction in effect: the two bytes as they stand disagree.

contradictions.title: CA-2 scopes argument vectors; argument-vector scoping is a RESERVED, NOT-DESIGNED extension point owned by DR-125
contradictions.measurement: Doctor CA-2 binds 'the exact argument vector, which is descriptor-controlled and never a shell string'. PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED's scopeParameter states 'Argument vectors are NOT scoped by this token; argument-level policy is not designed here and is a RESERVED extension point', and reserved point 4 assigns minting to 'DR-125, or a successor to this contract'.
contradictions.consequence: Doctor mints, under the word 'scopeBound', the policy surface DR-105 named as reserved and assigned to another row. This is item-2 vocabulary minting by semantic duplication, not by name collision.

contradictions.title: Doctor bounds consent with a WALL-CLOCK DEADLINE; DR-105 and DR-G09 forbid the clock deciding, and R-10 rules out exactly this evaluation
contradictions.measurement: Doctor CA-1 binds 'a wall-clock deadline'; CA-2/CA-3/CA-4 each bind 'a deadline' (measured: 9 occurrences of 'deadline', 2 of 'wall-clock', 0 of 'sequence number' in doctor). DR-105 R-10: 'Expiry is materialized as a journaled record at the sequence where the host observes it ... It is NOT evaluated by comparing a wall-clock expiry timestamp against a wall-clock now at commit time; doing so would make the clock the order, which DR-G09 forbids.' Register line 324, DR-G09 waiver-rule cell, measured at f0d72536...: 'wall-clock/component ordering is forbidden'.
contradictions.consequence: Under the join a doctor deadline must be materialized as an ordered record. Doctor writes no journal and holds no sequence numbers, so the deadline it specifies is the form DR-105 rules out. Either doctor's bound is not an expiry in DR-105's sense (and the pair has two incompatible expiry notions -- see TERM-8) or it is, and it is the forbidden shape.

contradictions.title: Doctor's CLOSED status set and CLOSED execution vocabulary have no carrier for DR-105's INDETERMINATE or COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION -- and forcing them into 'refused' is the exact mismodeling DR-105 forbids
contradictions.measurement: Doctor's status set is closed at five tokens with 'no sixth token may be added', and the consent record's `execution` member takes exactly file 03's three values 'enforced', 'disclosed-trusted-code', 'refused'. DR-105 makes INDETERMINATE 'a first-class value of this record, not an error path' (L-5) and states in notRefusals: 'INDETERMINATE is an OUTCOME, not a refusal ... Modeling it as a refusal would let a summary count it among the effects that did not happen', and the same 'with more force' for COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION. Measured: zero occurrences of 'irreversib' anywhere in doctor's bytes, against 40 in DR-105.
contradictions.consequence: A consented CA-4 egress that crashed between commit-intent and outcome is DR-105-INDETERMINATE. Doctor's record must then say 'refused' (false -- bytes may have left the host, and DR-105's own FX-6 is a wording-level golden against precisely this narration) or 'enforced' (false -- and doctor's own FC-CONSENT fails on it) or 'disclosed-trusted-code' (a statement about confinement, not about outcome). Every available value is wrong. This is the sharpest single defect in the pair: doctor's honesty machinery, which is otherwise excellent, has no slot for the honest answer DR-105 mandates.
contradictions.notMitigatedBy: The free-text `result` member. DR-105's disclosure obligations are stated as VALUES with verbatim vocabulary, and FX-6 exists because 'honest mechanics have historically been narrated away at the output layer'. Carrying INDETERMINATE in prose is that narration.

contradictions.title: DR-105 journals acceptance for every request including reads; doctor's FC-RO fails if any byte changes outside the Operational metadata class, under EVERY consent class
contradictions.measurement: DR-105: 'Reads still journal acceptance, because a read of a denied path is the refusal this token exists to record', over 'ONE durable, append-only grant journal per (project, grant generation)'. ID-DEP-P5 expressly refuses to assign the journal to Operational metadata: 'It does NOT assign the journal to operational metadata or to any other class, because that assignment is DR-124's.' Doctor FC-RO fails if 'any byte outside the Operational metadata class changed', and its variants require the property to hold 'with each consent class named, since consent to CA-1..CA-4 never departs from DP-1/DP-4'.
contradictions.consequence: If DR-124 places the grant journal anywhere but the Operational metadata class, FC-RO fails by construction on every consented doctor invocation -- and on every default invocation too, if doctor's reads journal. Two acceptance-evidence surfaces from two candidate contracts that can both be executed and that contradict, with the deciding row (DR-124) open on both sides.
contradictions.note: This is the one finding in this file that is mechanically testable the day both fixture surfaces exist. It should be routed before either row closes.

contradictions.title: MEASUREMENT / restatement-authorship: doctor asserts no DR-105 artifact exists, contradicting its own late-measurement record and the current bytes
contradictions.dr105Pointer: (subject file identity: docs/coop/artifacts/permission-truth-tables.v1.json, sha256 0f73f31cffccc85d10c71596f05ed1e00d044cff12b9ecf56a1aa8c44f973632, measured present at this review's start AND end)
contradictions.measurement: /whatThisDoesNotDo/2 reads in full: 'Does NOT mint a permission token, an effect class, or a platform truth-table entry. consentRecord.permissionRef is a reserved binding point riding DR-105 (ID-DEP-2), and no DR-105 artifact exists in the measured tree.' The final clause is unqualified and present-tense. /recordedInputs/lateMeasurementObservation/observation states the opposite for the same file at the same digest, and /recordedInputs/lateMeasurementObservation/discipline gives the reason the section exists: 'leaving an earlier measurement's phrasing standing would make a claim in this artifact false at the reviewer's measurement moment.'
contradictions.whyItIsAFindingEvenThoughTheConclusionSu: Freeze 7.2.2: a recited fact that does not replicate is a finding even when the conclusion survives. The conclusion (doctor mints no token) DOES survive and is independently verified here -- measured: zero matches for `PT-[A-Z-]+` anywhere in doctor's bytes. The recital does not. The artifact's own stated discipline was applied to one section and not to the other.
contradictions.notAnEnvironmentException: 7.8.1 covers a MISSING input presenting as a finding. This is the inverse: a PRESENT input asserted absent. The tree changing under an authoring session is environment; a sentence left standing that the session's own discipline required it to correct is authorship.
contradictions.deduplicationNote: The doctor-subject lane will likely also raise this. It is recorded here because the false clause is a claim about the OTHER side of the join.

sharedTermDisagreements.dr105: /permissionVocabulary/tokens/*/scopeParameter and /raceSemantics/races/8 -- a typed, per-token data parameter on a grant (path-prefix list, variable names, program identifiers, endpoint set, state class), journaled, with narrowing itself a record carrying its own sequence number so 'a grant's scope cannot change without a sequence number'.
sharedTermDisagreements.doctor: /consentModel/consentableActionClasses/*/scopeBound and /consentModel/mandatoryPostReport/recordMembers/3 -- a free-text bundle of invocation identity + check ids + target identity + resource enumeration + deadline + byte cap, held only for the invocation and never persisted.
sharedTermDisagreements.disagreement: Same word, different TYPE and different LIFETIME. DR-105 scope is durable data whose changes are ordered; doctor scope is an ephemeral report member. DR-105's PR-4 (scope-exceeded) is decidable only against the first kind.
sharedTermDisagreements.latentDefect: A joined implementation reading 'scope' from doctor's consent record cannot evaluate PR-4 against it.

sharedTermDisagreements.dr105: /truthTables/columnSemantics/GRANTED -- 'An AUTHORIZATION record. Resolution to granted, durably ordered. Confers PERMISSION, not CAPABILITY. On a DISCLOSURE-ONLY row it changes nothing about what the component can do.'
sharedTermDisagreements.doctor: /consentModel/mandatoryPostReport/recordMembers/6 -- the operator having named consent, after which doctor (the actor) proceeds. Doctor's 'granted' DOES change what happens, because doctor performs the act itself.
sharedTermDisagreements.disagreement: DR-105's central honesty rule is that GRANTED confers nothing operational; doctor's granted is operationally decisive. Both cite file 03's same two-record split as their source.
sharedTermDisagreements.latentDefect: A joined output that says 'granted' means two different things depending on which artifact's row the reader is looking at -- the exact confusion DR-105's /truthTables/columnSemantics/theRuleThisTableExistsToHold forbids.

sharedTermDisagreements.dr105: /truthTables/columnSemantics/ENFORCED and /truthTables/enforcementStateVocabulary -- a per-(platform, token, execution-mode) CELL value drawn from a FOUR-member vocabulary (ENFORCED-BY-CONSTRUCTION, ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, DISCLOSURE-ONLY, OPEN), each requiring a named mechanism and a stated scope of claim.
sharedTermDisagreements.doctor: /consentModel/mandatoryPostReport/recordMembers/7 -- a per-ACTION record value drawn from file 03's THREE-member execution vocabulary (enforced, disclosed-trusted-code, refused).
sharedTermDisagreements.disagreement: Doctor's three-value set cannot express ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER (route-only enforcement carrying a MANDATORY paired disclosure) or OPEN. DR-105's four-value set cannot express 'refused'. The two vocabularies overlap on one token ('enforced') and diverge on everything else.
sharedTermDisagreements.credit: Doctor's rule that 'recording enforced without measured confinement would be exactly the claim file 03's confinement-honesty section forbids', and FC-CONSENT's failsIf 'execution is recorded enforced with no measured confinement', are in exact agreement with DR-105's DISCLOSURE-ONLY discipline. The disagreement is in the vocabulary's SHAPE, not its honesty.

sharedTermDisagreements.dr105: /truthTables/columnSemantics/DISCLOSED and /truthTables/tables/*/rows/*/DISCLOSED -- a binding OBLIGATION on the host's machine output and audit, derived from the ENFORCED value, requiring 'the enforcement state above VERBATIM in its own vocabulary, never softened', affirmatively, with 'Silence is not disclosure'.
sharedTermDisagreements.doctor: residual limitation prose (/consentModel/mandatoryPostReport/recordMembers/9) and the two-tier redaction split (/redaction/twoTierStructure), where DISCLOSURE means 'a claim stated as disclosure rather than guarantee'.
sharedTermDisagreements.disagreement: Two different senses: an obligation on output content versus a standing downgrade of a claim. Doctor's report is the natural and probably the ONLY carrier for DR-105's DISCLOSED obligation, and doctor binds no member to it.
sharedTermDisagreements.trapCited: MENTIONING is not CARRYING. Doctor names disclosure honesty repeatedly and binds no report member to DR-105's per-cell disclosure obligation; DR-105 states the obligation and names no surface that carries it.

sharedTermDisagreements.doctor: /degradedAndHostileInputs (DEG-4) and /identityDependencies/5 (ID-DEP-6) -- component/index signature revocation state, read as a RECORDED value, riding DR-112.

Doctor's /consentModel/dr105Join/whatThisContractDefines/4 enumerates five file-03 laws it says hold regardless of which tokens DR-105 mints and OMITS this one -- the file-03 law most directly governing its own subject.

scenarioWalks.name: MANDATED WALK: user consents to an egress probe; the probe starts; the grant is revoked mid-probe
scenarioWalks.setup: Operator names CA-4 consent for a TRUST-STATE revocation-refresh check, endpoint set enumerated, byte budget set, deadline set. Doctor opens the socket. A revocation lands while bytes are in flight.
scenarioWalks.whyNot: The pair offers TWO readings and supplies no selector. DR-105 /tensionsObserved/2 (T-3) states the fork in its own words: 'Is a doctor probe's named consent a GRANT in the permission journal (and therefore revocable, expiring, and linearized like any other), or a separate DR-114 record with its own lifecycle? The two readings differ observably: only the first makes a consented probe revocable mid-operation with a linearization point, and only the first puts it in the audit binding file 03 specifies.' DR-105 declines to choose and assigns the choice to 'DR-114's owner (Operability + security), jointly with the DR-105 row's owner'. Doctor -- the DR-114 candidate -- also declines, listing 'the grant-revocation linearization semantics' at /consentModel/dr105Join/whatThisContractDoesNotDefine/2 as DR-105's. CIRCULAR DEFERRAL.

readingA.assume: The consent IS a journal grant.
readingA.walk: REQUEST-ACCEPTED (RA) at sequence a -> IRREVERSIBLE-COMMIT-INTENT (ICI) at n, durable BEFORE the first byte leaves (PT-NET-EGRESS is IRREVERSIBLE by class rule) -> REVOCATION (REV) at r. If n < r: COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION, disclosed and not reported undone (R-3, /linearization/irreversibleBoundary/caseBefore). If the ICI is not yet durable: r < n is unreachable, the effect is never initiated, PR-5 (R-1/R-2).
readingA.whatBreaks: Doctor writes no journal, holds no sequence numbers, mints no identity (ID-DEP-10), and its consent 'expires with the invocation and is never persisted'. DR-105's durability rule (/linearization/theOrder/durabilityRule) is explicit: 'A sequence number assigned in memory but not yet durable orders NOTHING and gates NOTHING.' An unjournaled doctor consent therefore gates nothing, so under reading A the consent cannot authorize the egress at all. Further, AUD (L-8) binds to grant generation, process descendant, Run/operation, and broker request IDs -- doctor has none of the four. And CONTRA-7 fires: the journal writes may violate FC-RO.

readingB.assume: The consent is a doctor-side record with its own lifecycle.
readingB.walk: There is no r. Nothing bars the probe. It runs to its deadline or its byte budget and a consent record is written.
readingB.whatBreaks: DR-105 states the consequence itself: 'If the second reading wins, PT-NET-EGRESS's slice-1 posture re-binds to DR-114's record and this contract's journal position for it is withdrawn.' The single token the join actually supplies then loses the linearization DR-105 exists to provide, and the DR-105 row's own acceptance evidence ('durable monotonic ordering of request acceptance ... revocation, cleanup, and audit', register line 268, measured) has no doctor content. Mid-probe revocation becomes UNDEFINED on both sides.

scenarioWalks.name: MANDATED WALK: an irreversible doctor action
scenarioWalks.doesOneExist: YES -- three. Under DR-105's byToken rulings, CA-4 egress is IRREVERSIBLE by class rule that no declaration may override; CA-1 and CA-2 are irreversible because 'The host holds no inverse for whatever a spawned process did before it was reaped' (PT-PROC-EXEC-DECLARED).
scenarioWalks.walk: DR-105 requires ICI durable BEFORE initiation (L-4: 'THIS RECORD IS THE EFFECT-COMMIT POINT'), then ICO recording COMPLETED, FAILED, or INDETERMINATE. Doctor initiates a CA-1 spawn or a CA-4 send with no pre-commit record of any kind -- 'irreversib' occurs zero times in its bytes -- and writes ONE consent record after the fact, whose `execution` value is constrained to three options none of which can be INDETERMINATE (CONTRA-6).
scenarioWalks.crashCase: Host dies between ICI and ICO. DR-105: recovery records ICO = INDETERMINATE, discloses it, does not guess, does not retry ('assume failed then retry ... converts an unknown single effect into a known double effect'), and the generation is treated as revoked fail-closed. Doctor: the report was never emitted, so outcome class OC-5 (doctorFault) -- which says the SINK failed and says nothing about whether the egress landed. The two answers are not merely different; doctor's is silent on the only fact DR-105 requires be disclosed.
scenarioWalks.verdict: NO deterministic answer, and doctor's report structure cannot carry DR-105's. BLK-3.

scenarioWalks.name: MANDATED WALK: a probe that outlives its grant
scenarioWalks.doctorAnswer: The deadline on the consent scope bounds it; exceeding a bound yields UNDETERMINED with cause observation-bounded (/degradedAndHostileInputs, BOUNDED READS rule). Evaluated against wall-clock at action time.
scenarioWalks.dr105Answer: Nothing expires until an EXPIRY RECORD is ordered in the journal at the sequence where the host observes it, whereupon it behaves as REV; and comparing wall-clock expiry to wall-clock now at commit time is expressly ruled out because 'doing so would make the clock the order, which DR-G09 forbids' (R-10). The register's DR-G09 waiver cell, measured this session at line 324, reads 'wall-clock/component ordering is forbidden'.
scenarioWalks.divergence: Doctor's mechanism is the one DR-105 names as the wrong one, and DR-105's mechanism needs a journal doctor does not have. A probe that runs past its deadline is terminated by doctor and, by DR-105, has not expired at all until a record says so.

scenarioWalks.name: SUPPLEMENTARY WALK (worth recording): default doctor invocation, no consent named
scenarioWalks.deterministic: PARTIALLY -- and the partial answer is itself the finding.
scenarioWalks.walk: Doctor reads the installed generation inventory, component index custody records, other components' admitted manifest metadata, project strict configuration, the project lock, and the allowlisted environment layer; then writes its own audit record inside the Operational metadata class. Under DR-105's tables those are PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT, PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-ENV-READ and PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE respectively. Doctor names none of them and gates none of them: its four default properties are asserted as properties, not as permissions.
scenarioWalks.ifDoctorIsSubjectToTheVocabulary: Absence denies (/permissionVocabulary/closure, PR-1). Doctor declares no tokens anywhere, so its ENTIRE default posture is DENIED and doctor cannot run at all.
scenarioWalks.ifDoctorIsNotSubjectToTheVocabulary: Then CA-1..CA-4 are equally outside it, and doctor's TOTAL-mapping requirement (/consentModel/dr105Join/theJoinExactly/cardinalityIsDr105s) is unsatisfiable in principle rather than pending DR-105's closure.
scenarioWalks.verdict: The pair forces a dilemma with no third branch. This is the root cause stated as a walk. BLK-6.

scenarioWalks.name: SUPPLEMENTARY WALK: CA-1 probe of a component whose declared posture is networked, no CA-4 named
scenarioWalks.walk: Doctor REFUSES (/consentModel/consentDoesNotCascade/theHardCase: 'consenting to CA-1 or CA-2 for a target whose declared posture includes network REQUIRES a separately named CA-4 consent, and if CA-4 is absent the action is REFUSED rather than executed-and-hoped'). DR-105 agrees in substance: PT-NET-EGRESS DENIED by absence, and DISCLOSURE-ONLY in every one of its four cells, so no mechanism would have contained the spawned process -- which is exactly why refusing rather than executing is the only honest posture.
scenarioWalks.verdict: THE JOIN CLOSES HERE, cleanly, in both directions. Two blind lanes reached the same answer from opposite ends. Recorded under whatWorksWell/W-5.

semanticFindings.concept: byte budget / byte cap as a consent bound
semanticFindings.dr105Comparison: No DR-105 token carries a quantitative volume parameter; every scopeParameter is an enumeration of NAMES (path prefixes, variable names, program identifiers, endpoint sets, state class). A volume allowance is a permission-shaped bound minted under a different word.
semanticFindings.note: Doctor's cardinalityIsDr105s clause covers 'a token plus a scope expression', which arguably reserves room for it -- but a scope expression DR-105 has no grammar for is not reserved, it is invented.

semanticFindings.dr105Comparison: RESERVED, NOT DESIGNED at /permissionVocabulary/reservedExtensionPoints/3, minting assigned to DR-125.
DR-105 has expiry as a journaled record (R-10) and no wall-clock deadline concept.

semanticFindings.concept: CA-1..CA-4 as compound action classes each spanning several DR-105 effect classes
semanticFindings.assessment: NOT A DEFECT ON ITS OWN. Doctor declares them 'DOCTOR-SIDE, SURFACE-LOCAL action-class identities -- the same status the control-protocol candidate's RF-* families hold on their plane. They are carriers, not permissions.' That idiom is precedented in this corpus and DR-105 uses the mirror of it for PR-1..PR-9. The defect is not the idiom; it is that CA-3 in particular spans four effects of which none has a token (GAP-2, GAP-3, CONTRA-2, CONTRA-3), so no cardinality decision can resolve it.

vocabularyMinting.conclusion: Doctor honored the LETTER of the 'ride DR-105's vocabulary, do not mint your own' requirement completely and verifiably. It minted three permission-shaped SCOPE concepts (byte budget, argument vector, wall-clock deadline) that DR-105 either reserved or has no grammar for. That is minting by semantic duplication under a different word, which the review brief names as the defect.

readOnlyEffectTension.question: Is there any doctor default behaviour DR-105's tables would classify as requiring a grant, or any DR-105 token whose absence would silently disable a doctor default?

findings.detail: FOUR. Doctor's default reads map to PT-FS-READ-PROJECT, PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT and PT-ENV-READ; doctor's one permitted write maps to PT-FS-WRITE-HOST-STATE. None is consent-gated in doctor and none is referenced. Under DR-105's absence-denies closure, doctor's 'default' is a fully permissioned action set. See SCEN-4 and MISS-1..MISS-3.

findings.detail: PT-FS-READ-COMPONENT's own slice justification is that splitting it from PT-FS-READ-PROJECT 'keeps a project-read denial from silently disabling a component's own closure'. Doctor writes host state that is allocated to no component and reads OTHER components' trees. The tokens as worded cannot express either act. Neither artifact could see this alone.

residualFindingsOnThisAxis.finding: INVERTED PROBLEM. If CA-4 resolves to PT-NET-EGRESS, DR-105's DISCLOSED cell obliges the host to tell the operator 'that this component is trusted code in the TCB for this effect class and that the grant record is a record of asking, not of confinement'. Applied to doctor's own egress that disclosure is FALSE: doctor controls its own sockets, and doctor says so at /namedDifferencesFromPrototype (DIFF-6): 'doctor's default must be a statement about DOCTOR, which is enforceable because doctor controls its own sockets.' The join forces an UNDER-claim -- a mandatory false disclosure over a genuinely enforced act.

DR-105's DISCLOSED obligation has NO carrier. It is an obligation on 'the machine output and the audit'. Doctor's report is the machine output and binds no member to it. Neither artifact names who emits the per-cell enforcement string. MENTIONING is not CARRYING, on both sides.

Doctor's three-value execution vocabulary cannot express ENFORCED-AT-HOST-BROKER, which DR-105 defines as route-only enforcement carrying a MANDATORY paired disclosure. Recording it as 'enforced' would drop the mandatory pairing; recording it as 'disclosed-trusted-code' would drop the enforcement. Currently moot (doctor uses no broker, MISS-4) and would bite the moment it did.

whatWorksWell.finding: NEITHER ARTIFACT CONFERS STANDING ON THE OTHER. Both headers verified at current bytes: status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, reviewStatus AWAITING-INDEPENDENT-REVIEW, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, version 1, date 2026-08-13, identical on both. Doctor's /recordedInputs/lateMeasurementObservation/standingAndConsequence explicitly refuses to consume DR-105's candidate and gives the right reason: 'Consuming an unreviewed candidate's token vocabulary would be exactly the failure the reserved-binding-point idiom exists to prevent.' DR-105 for its part cites the doctor obligation from file 04's bytes, not from any candidate. There is no circular appliedness anywhere in the pair.

THE PRIMARY REQUIREMENT IS HONORED AND VERIFIABLE. Doctor was required to ride DR-105's vocabulary rather than mint its own. Measured: zero permission tokens of any name in doctor's bytes; zero consent grammar in DR-105's bytes; each defers the other's half in writing (DR-105 /permissionVocabulary/tokens/4/scopeParameter 'DR-114 owns the consent contract'; doctor /consentModel/dr105Join/whatThisContractDoesNotDefine). Two blind lanes drew the same line in the same place.

THE ENDPOINT-GRAMMAR DEPENDENCY ACTUALLY CLOSES. DR-105: 'Endpoint set as named by the consent record. This artifact does not design the endpoint grammar.' Doctor: CA-4 is bound to 'the exact endpoint or endpoint set ... enumerated, never a pattern', with `endpoint` a required, nullable-with-reason record member and FC-POSTREPORT asserting 'the recorded endpoint equals the contacted one'. DR-105's PR-4 (scope-exceeded) explicitly covers 'an endpoint outside the consent record'. This one join is complete, non-circular, and testable. It is the proof that the join CAN be made -- it just was not made for the other three action classes.

IDENTICAL FAIL-CLOSED DIRECTION. DR-105: absence denies, deny wins, closure means an unknown token is a refusal not an ignore. Doctor: 'an action class with no resolved token is UNEXERCISABLE ... fail-closed, never permitted-by-default', and the reduced form IS the default posture, 'a complete, useful, and honest product'. When the join fails, both artifacts fail in the safe direction. This is why the seven blockers are correctness/coherence defects rather than security defects.

THE SAME HONESTY CONCLUSION REACHED BLIND FROM OPPOSITE ENDS. DR-105 computes 24/28 DISCLOSURE-ONLY and writes 'The ratio is the point, not an embarrassment.' Doctor writes 'the no-egress property is DECLARED and not enforced by doctor' as a MANDATORY residual limitation on every such action and refuses the networked-target case outright. SCEN-5 walks cleanly end to end. Two independent lanes, one discipline.

DR-105 PREDICTED THIS JOIN DEFECT IN WRITING. /tensionsObserved/2 (T-3) names the exact fork this review's scenario walks fail on, names both readings, names how they differ observably, states what it did pending resolution, and assigns resolution to 'DR-114's owner (Operability + security), jointly with the DR-105 row's owner'. It also states the consequence of the reading doctor implicitly took. The corpus's tension-reporting discipline did its job; what is missing is only the coordinator act it asked for.

Verified at current bytes this session: file 03 line 102 four-part consent binding; file 04 lines 226-234 doctor paragraph; register DR-105 at line 268, DR-114 at line 277, DR-G09 waiver-rule cell at line 324; DR-105's 28/24/2/2 enforcement census and its per-platform 5/7/1/1 breakdown, recomputed mechanically; doctor's restatement of DR-105's header fields (artifact name, documentClass, registerRow, status, reviewStatus, sealRecommendation, binds) and its digest prefix 0f73f31c. advisories.advisory: DO NOT APPLY THE PAIR TOGETHER as it stands. Applying DR-105 alone is coherent (its doctor-facing statements ride DR-114's ROW and survive). Applying DR-114 alone is coherent (permissionRef stays reserved and the default posture is complete without any token). Applying BOTH activates GAP-0 and the seven blockers simultaneously and there is no disposition text in either artifact that resolves them.

THE ONE DECISION THAT UNBLOCKS THE MOST. Answer the ACTOR question first: are HOST surfaces (doctor, and by extension every other host-initiated act under direct user instruction) subject to the DR-105 vocabulary at all? DR-105's own fourth non-token already contains the principle for the negative answer; it simply was not generalized. A NO answer dissolves GAP-0, TENSION-RO-1..3, MISS-1..MISS-3, SCEN-4, and reduces the join to 'doctor's consent is a doctor-side record' -- which is DR-105's T-3 reading B, whose stated price is that PT-NET-EGRESS's journal position is withdrawn. A YES answer requires doctor to acquire a manifest-equivalent, a journal position, and grant-generation identity, none of which exist. NO is the cheaper and, on DR-105's own reasoning, the more principled answer.

IF READING B IS CHOSEN, three items must be routed explicitly rather than left to fall out: (i) what supplies DR-105's DISCLOSED obligation for doctor's actions (ENF-2); (ii) where INDETERMINATE and COMPLETED-BEFORE-REVOCATION land in doctor's CLOSED status set, which cannot absorb them without a schema break doctor's stability rules forbid (CONTRA-6); (iii) whether CA-2 survives at all given reserved point 6 (CONTRA-1), since that decides whether the DECIDED D-008/DR-119 exception has a doctor carrier.

Two items I noticed that are yours, not mine, recorded so they are not lost: (a) /truthTables/tables/*/rows/*/GRANTED describes the grant tuple as 'file 03's binding list, carried whole' but drops file 03 line 105's first member ('Request/Execution attempt') and splits its 'component/generation' into two -- a restatement-authorship question on a phrase that is load-bearing for the join (GAP-4 depends on it); (b) /enforcedColumnCensus/openDeterminationsCarriedSeparately/futureEnforcementPrimitive counts 12 of 14 child-process cells as OPEN on a future primitive while /enforcedColumnCensus/honestyRatio counts 4 of 28 as enforced -- arithmetically consistent (14-2=12, the two broker cells being route-only) but the two counts read as inconsistent on a fast pass. Neither is a join finding.

CONTRA-8 (/whatThisDoesNotDo/2) is yours as much as mine; deduplicate. Separately: /consentModel/dr105Join/whatThisContractDefines/4 enumerates five file-03 laws and omits the one governing its own subject (consent bound to component bytes, operation, scope, platform, file 03 line 102). Not a token mint, so not a violation of your standing instruction -- but it is the file-03 law your four scope bounds most needed to carry, and none of them carries 'platform'.

ASYMMETRIC AWARENESS IS ENVIRONMENT, NOT A FINDING (7.8.1). DR-105 measured file 04's doctor paragraph and could not measure a doctor candidate that did not exist; doctor measured DR-105's candidate late and correctly refused to consume it. Neither is at fault for not citing the other. Every finding above is stated over the two artifacts' CURRENT BYTES and would stand regardless of authoring order.
